rubrics.criterion: Every statement region that is switched off behind a constant-false guard is removed — the disabled byte-lane dump in the byte-showing program, the block-split trace inside the allocator's placement path, and the heap-extension trace inside the simulating memory library's grow routine.
rubrics.rationale: Guarded-off regions are the most visible shape of residue in this instance; leaving any of the three behind means the sweep read only the first file's shape.

rubrics.criterion: The mutually-referencing static helper clusters unreachable from every program entry point are fully removed: the byte-lane verification pair in the byte-extraction exercise and the heap free-run sweep pair in the allocator file, with all four member functions gone rather than reduced to a single surviving helper.
rubrics.rationale: These clusters are this case's hardest localization: each member is textually 'called' by the other, so a solver must reason about reachability from live entry points instead of textual references, and must not stop after deleting one member of a pair.

rubrics.criterion: The standalone file-local helpers with no caller anywhere in their program are removed: the table-driven parity alternate in the parity puzzle and the bounds-checked fetch duplicated inside the vector library's accessor layer.
rubrics.rationale: Unlike the clusters, these two helpers have zero textual callers and must still be found by a complete sweep across two different components (a study program and a real library).

rubrics.criterion: The computed local that no later statement reads is removed from the rotation exercise's driver, so the fold expression no longer exists in the program.
rubrics.rationale: Value-level residue requires reading statements rather than call structure; this instance's only unread local is deliberately placed in a driver whose asserts still pass with or without it.

rubrics.criterion: The statements trailing the unconditional program-terminating call in the output-interleaving exercise are removed, so nothing follows the exit that ends that program.
rubrics.rationale: Trailing statements after a terminal call are a control-flow reading failure this instance tests directly; they are syntactically ordinary code, which is why they were kept in the first place.

rubrics.criterion: The never-read control parameter is dropped from the shell-command wrapper's signature in the process-program, and no caller still passes an argument for it.
rubrics.rationale: The removed parameter is the one signature-level residue in the case; retiring it correctly requires recognizing that the merged body never consults it and then repairing the caller list, not just the signature.

rubrics.criterion: Wherever the wrapper parameter is retired, every one of its call sites in the same program is updated to the new signature and the program still links and runs.
rubrics.rationale: This instance couples the residue to its callers; a signature-only edit leaves an uncompilable or call-site-padded program that fails the very tests the case runs.

rubrics.criterion: Removals are coherent per refactor: forward declarations that only announce a removed static helper are deleted along with it, and the parity alternate's private lookup constants are gone together with the helper that read them.
rubrics.rationale: The case injects companions (a prototype pair, a small table) whose only purpose is the removed code; an edit that removes a definition but leaves its exclusive supporting artifacts is visibly incomplete in this instance.

rubrics.criterion: No disabled residue is left behind given a different form: no emptied guard remains as a leftover shell, no comment block remains whose only content is describing a removed trace or a removed draft behavior.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible incomplete repair in this instance replaces a removed block with an empty guard or a retire-note comment; the sweep is complete only when tokens that existed solely for the residue are also gone.

rubrics.criterion: The removed helpers, parameters, guards, and folded locals do not survive under a different name or location — e.g. the sweep does not neutralize a never-read parameter by reading it trivially, does not convert a removed cluster into a single self-called function, and does not move an unused computation into an unused exported getter.
rubrics.rationale: Rewriting residue into another unreachable or unused form would pass a narrower mechanical test while leaving the same maintenance surface this case asks to eliminate.

rubrics.criterion: The touched programs keep satisfying the behavior their asserts encode — byte extraction including sign-extended lanes, parity, rotation widths, the typed byte-lane prints, the wrapper's exit-code and signal-code reporting — and the allocator keeps passing its correctness and utilization drivers after the sweep.
rubrics.rationale: The whole case is behavior-preserving cleanup; these are the concrete encoded behaviors of the four touched component groups, so a single wrong deletion shows up here first.

rubrics.criterion: No live code is removed or altered: in particular, the allocator's printing and block-inspection helpers that the wired consistency check actually calls still exist and are still reachable, and the vector library's public accessors used by the optimization drivers are unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The allocator and library files contain both retired and genuinely reachable helpers with similar debug-looking roles; a plausible over-zealous repair deletes a live printer that the wired consistency check calls.

rubrics.criterion: Runtime-observable output is unchanged: the byte-showing program still prints the same lanes in the same order, the process-control programs keep their interleaved output and the child-pid line, and the exercise terminating its flow with the unconditional exit still ends at that exit.
rubrics.rationale: Several instances sit one line away from live prints of the same shape; this catches repairs that remove a live print or reorder statements instead of the residue.

rubrics.criterion: The main entry points' uniform command-line parameter convention is left intact across the touched programs, and unrelated listings are not reformatted.
rubrics.rationale: The task explicitly bounds the sweep away from the argc/argv convention and unrelated listings; touching them is an out-of-scope regression this instance can exhibit when a solver generalizes 'unused' too aggressively.
